q-183454.name: Question 6
q-183454.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ For all $n\in N,$ ${n}^{2}$ is not prime.
q-183454.worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(n):{n}^{2}\text{ is prime},
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∀n\in N,\,¬P(n).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∀n\in N,\,¬P(n)) & ≡∃n\in N,\,¬¬P(n) \\  & ≡∃n\in N,\,\text{ }P(n).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $∃n\in N,\,P(n)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **There exists** $n\in N$ such that ${n}^{2}$ is prime.

q-183466.name: Question 13
q-183466.problem:
Negate the following statement:

$\,$ There exists $x\in C$ such that ${x}^{2}$ is not positive.
q-183466.worked_solution:
If we denote

$$
P(x):{x}^{2}\text{ is positive},
$$

our statement can be written as

$$
∃x\in C,\,¬P(x).
$$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃x\in C,\,¬P(x)) & ≡∀x\in C,\,¬¬P(x) \\  & ≡∀x\in C,\,P(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $∀x\in C,\,P(x)$ reads as follows:

$\,$ **For all** $x\in C,$ ${x}^{2}$ is positive.

Question 14
?

Negate the following statement:

There exists n∈N such that 2n is not composite.

a
There exists n∈N such that 2n is not composite.
b
There exists n∈N such that 2n is composite.
c
None of the listed
d
For all n∈N, 2n is composite.
e
For all n∈N, 2n is not composite.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If we denote P(n):2n is composite,

our statement can be written as ∃n∈N,¬P(n).

Negating this, we obtain ¬(∃n∈N,¬P(n))≡∀n∈N,¬¬P(n)≡∀n∈N,P(n).

Finally, ∀n∈N,P(n) reads as follows:

For all n∈N, 2n is composite.

q-216698.problem:
Negate the following statement: 

$\,$ At least one existential statement is not true.
q-216698.worked_solution:
Let $E$ be the set of all existential statements. The given statement can be re-phrased as follows:

$\,$ There exists $S\in E$ such that $S$ is not true.

Introducing the existential quantifier, we get the following:

$\,$ $∃S\in E,\,S\text{ is not true}.$

Negating this, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(∃S\in E,\,S\text{ is not true}) & ≡∀S\in E,\,¬(S\text{ is not true}) \\  & ≡∀S\in E,\,S\text{ is true}\end{aligned}
$$

which reads 

$\,$ For all $S\in E,$ $S$ is true.

or simply

$\,$ Every existential statement is true.
